how_to_read_this: Every listing was checked against the publisher's own page on the `verified` date. A catalog of
local models is out of date in weeks: before you propose one, open its Ollama library page or its
Hugging Face repo and confirm the tag and the size are still there, and say that you did.
status 'verified-here' means the model was actually run on this machine, through Relay, and passed
scripts/relay-local.py smoke. status 'unverified-listing' means the page says so and nothing more.
The smoke test decides, not this file. download_gb is what comes down the wire; memory_gb is what
the weights hold once loaded and is null wherever the publisher does not state it - the context
window (-c / num_ctx) often costs more than the weights do.
tiers are the machine's usable memory in GB (unified memory counts; leave the desktop 40-60 GB on a
128 GB machine). A model in a lower tier runs on a bigger machine too.

8.name: Granite 4.2 8B

flags.note: Tool calls are emitted as XML (<tool_call><function=...><parameter=...>), not JSON. Reasoning needs the granite_thinking_parser.py plugin on vLLM.

8.warning: The ollama.com/library/granite4.2 page shows no `tools` capability badge, unlike granite4 and granite4.1. Run the smoke test before promising tool calling through Ollama.

8.name: Ornith 1.5 9B
8.licence: MIT (frontmatter; the repo ships no LICENSE file and the license_link 404s)

flags.note: Tool arguments are XML per-parameter tags, not JSON. Thinking is on by default and lands in content as <think> unless a reasoning parser splits it (llama.cpp: --reasoning-format deepseek).

8.warning: ollama.com has a separate, older `ornith` entry as well as `ornith-1.5`. Pull the tag deliberately.

16.name: gpt-oss-20b
16.quant: MXFP4 (the weights ship quantised; this is not a quant choice)

flags.note: Trained on OpenAI's harmony response format and, in the card's words, will not work correctly without it. Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp and Transformers apply it for you; a hand-rolled client must not. Reasoning effort is low/medium/high.

16.name: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B

flags.note: Runs on the PrismML fork only. Stock llama.cpp rejects PQ2_0/PTQ1_0 outright, and loads a plain Q2_0 build of the same weights without a warning and produces garbage. Upstream support is an open PR, not merged.

16.measured_here: DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64), -c 131072: ~17 GiB resident awake, ~3 GiB asleep, 1.6 s to wake, ~24 tok/s decode. smoke 2026-09-18: checks 1,2,3,5 pass, check 4 fails (the server's parser turns a literal <tool_call> in prose into a tool call).

24.name: Muse Glimmer 30B

flags.llamacpp: --jinja (the card calls it non-optional); needs a build of b10353 or newer; never stop on <|eom|>; register with --tool-arguments-as-object: the model's chat template raises "requires tool_call.function.arguments to be a dict (mapping)" on the JSON-string arguments a client replays, so the second turn of a tool conversation fails without it
flags.note: Reasoning cannot be turned off, only tuned with reasoning_strength. Dense, ~29.6B, with a vision tower that needs the separate mmproj file only for images. One tool call per turn: Meta's prompting guide says parallel tool calls are not supported, which matches Relay's default of parallel_tool_calls: false.
flags.ollama: no endpoint flags (Ollama renders the template itself)

24.measured_here: Through Ollama (muse-glimmer:latest, 18 GB, ~17 GiB resident, CONTEXT 131072) on 2026-09-18: smoke 5/5, no endpoint flags needed. Slow on this machine: 18-100 s per check. Not run here on llama.cpp: the --tool-arguments-as-object requirement comes from the template's own text, not from a run.

24.name: Qwen3.8 27B
24.quant: Q4_K_M (Ollama tag; the Qwen org publishes no official GGUF for this generation)

flags.note: The model card documents thinking (enable_thinking, reasoning_effort xhigh/medium/low) but says nothing at all about tool calling: no parser flag, no argument format. Multimodal. Treat tool use as unproven until the smoke test says otherwise.

24.name: Ornith 1.5 35B-A3B
24.licence: MIT (frontmatter; no LICENSE file in the repo)

flags.note: 3B active of 35B: fast for its size. XML tool arguments, as the 9B.

24.warning: The 9B and the 35B have different publisher sampling recipes. Do not copy one to the other.

48.name: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B
48.quant: Q4_0 (18.9 GB) on Hugging Face; the Ollama tag is 25 GB
48.licence: OpenMDW-1.1 (not Apache-2.0, not the NVIDIA Open Model License)

flags.note: Interleaved Mamba-2 + MoE, 3B active. The 1M window is the reason for the tier: the weights are small, the KV cache is not. Serve it at 256K unless the user asks for more.

128.name: Laguna S 2.1
128.quant: NVFP4 (66 GB). Q4_K_M is 96 GB - poolside's own README table says 68 GB, and the blob listing, the tree and Ollama all say 96 GB.

flags.note: 118B total, ~8B active, built for agentic coding. The GGUFs ship configured for 256K and poolside recommends staying there; 1M needs YaRN flags and costs quality. Ollama states a 128 GB unified-memory minimum, 13-18 tok/s, and OLLAMA_LOAD_TIMEOUT=20m. Mainline llama.cpp support for S 2.1 specifically is unconfirmed.

128.name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
128.quant: NVFP4 (105 GB). Q4_K_M is 120 GB, which leaves a 128 GB machine nothing.

flags.note: 125B with 6B activated, plus n-gram embeddings. The card documents thinking but not tool calling. Ollama calls it an experimental preview of the architecture behind Qwen4. At 105 GB on a 128 GB machine the desktop has almost nothing left: warn the user and check free memory first.

excluded.name: Llama 4
excluded.why: The Llama 4 Community License is not an open licence (700M-MAU trigger, naming and attribution rules) and the repos are gated; the smallest local build is 67 GB and neither the card nor the Ollama page mentions tool calling.

excluded.name: Phi-4
excluded.why: MIT and small, but the card never mentions tool or function calling and its chat template defines no tool role: there is no native tool calling to build an agent on.

excluded.name: BitNet b1.58 2B-4T
excluded.why: 4K context, no tool calling documented, and the efficiency only exists in the separate bitnet.cpp runtime, which offers no OpenAI-compatible server.

left_out_as_unverified: Whether llama.cpp's raw-text fallback for Muse Glimmer (its issue 27025, about one tool call in five) keeps the <atem:function_calls> wrapper: the issue shows the error, not the text. Relay's recovery accepts it with or without.
Memory held while loaded, for most entries: publishers give download sizes and sometimes a VRAM target, rarely a resident figure.
Tool-calling mechanics for both Qwen3.8 models, and general sampling for gpt-oss-20b and Laguna S 2.1: absent from the cards.
Minimum llama.cpp and Ollama versions for Ornith 1.5, Granite 4.2 and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning.
